classification.difficultyReason: Combine parallel-line angle relationships with adjacent angles, right angles and straight angles.

content.prompt: Find the value of $\alpha$ in each diagram below.

spec.description: Two solid horizontal parallels and a red dashed auxiliary parallel, with matching rightward parallel marks. Two sloping segments meet at the central vertex. The 50-degree label denotes the whole angle between them.
spec.mathematics: The upper sloping segment makes 20 degrees with a horizontal parallel; the complete central angle is 50 degrees; alpha is the lower-right angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 20 degrees, 50 degrees and the unknown alpha are visible.

answer.worked:
The angle above the dashed line at the central vertex is $20^\circ$ (alternate angles, upper line parallel to dashed line). The angle below the dashed line equals $\alpha$ (alternate angles, lower line parallel to dashed line).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+20^\circ&=50^\circ\quad\text{(adjacent angles)}\\\alpha&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right-angled triangle on a horizontal base extended right. The left side and the upper-right ray from the right base vertex carry matching parallel arrows.
spec.mathematics: Left base angle 55 degrees; top angle 90 degrees; unknown alpha at the right base. The additional ray is parallel to the left side.
spec.answerVisibility: The 55-degree given, right-angle square and alpha are visible; no derived angle is supplied.

answer.worked:
At the right base vertex, the angle between the extra ray and the rightward base extension is $55^\circ$ (corresponding angles, marked sloping lines parallel). The angle between the extra ray and the side leading to the top vertex is $90^\circ$ (co-interior angles, marked sloping lines parallel).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+90^\circ+55^\circ&=180^\circ\quad\text{(straight angle)}\\\alpha&=35^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two oblique transversals cross on the red dashed middle parallel, extending beyond the crossing to the left. Matching parallel arrows occur on all three horizontal lines.
spec.mathematics: The rising transversal makes 30 degrees with the top horizontal; the falling transversal makes 35 degrees with the bottom horizontal. Alpha denotes the complete left-hand angle at their crossing.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two supplied numerical angles and alpha are visible.

answer.worked:
The two angles on the right of the crossing, above and below the dashed parallel, are $30^\circ$ and $35^\circ$ respectively (alternate angles, each outer horizontal parallel to the dashed line). Their sum equals $\alpha$ (vertically opposite angles).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=30^\circ+35^\circ\\\alpha&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upper and lower horizontal rays are parallel to a dashed red horizontal through the central vertex. A descending segment extends straight through the central vertex to the upper-left. Alpha lies between this extension and the segment rising to the upper ray.
spec.mathematics: The upper interior angle is 123 degrees and the lower interior angle is 150 degrees. Alpha is the exterior angle at the central vertex, not the angle between the two rightward sloping segments.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 123 degrees, 150 degrees and alpha are supplied.

answer.worked:
The angle between the rising segment and the rightward dashed line is $180^\circ-123^\circ=57^\circ$ (co-interior angles, upper line parallel to dashed line). The angle between the descending segment and the rightward dashed line is $180^\circ-150^\circ=30^\circ$ (co-interior angles, lower line parallel to dashed line).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+57^\circ+30^\circ&=180^\circ\quad\text{(straight angle)}\\\alpha&=93^\circ\end{align*}$$
